nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Arre, beta. Out of the cell already?

choice.text: You said exactly the same thing yesterday.
You never painted over my wall.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Bhosle. Tier three. Thirty-one years in this building, and my knees remember every one of them.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Breakfast is at seven. Keep your head down and your hands where they can see them.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: Good morning, beta. Sleep well? Same words, same cup. Every time.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Did I? Old men repeat themselves, beta. Ask my wife.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: ...They give us a card with the words printed on it. Same breakfast, same keys on the same hooks. I'm not supposed to tell you that either.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Drink your chai while it's hot.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: The wall in my cell. You've seen what's scratched on it. You never painted over it.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Paint costs money, beta. The state is poor.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Some things a man should be allowed to keep. Even if he keeps forgetting where he put them.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Go, go. And don't make me run, haan? Not at my age.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Not so loud, beta. Tonight even the walls are on duty.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Drink your chai. All of it. Don't leave the cup lying about.

nodes.speaker: BHOSLE
nodes.text: Two o'clock. I'll take the long way round. My knees, you know.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Back again? You can't keep away from me, yaar.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: Do I know you?

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: This is the {kabir_time} time you've asked me that.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Kabir. S-03. I'd shake your hand, but the glass is very particular about that.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Their medicine stopped working on me years ago. So I remember. Every cycle. Yours too. Cycle {cycle_words}, and you still walk like you're late for something.

choice.text: Who is doing this to us?
Her name is Varma. Dr. M. Varma.
Why do you remember, and I don't?
What's in the room next to yours?
How do I get out of here?

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: A woman behind a pane of glass, two floors under Security. She watches you sit in the chair. She looks more tired every time.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: You know her name. You just keep losing it. Find it on paper, Parth. They write everything down in this place.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Arre, fine. Three cycles of watching you look for it is enough. Varma. Dr. Meera Varma.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Meera Varma. Good. Now the part you never like.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: She had a brother. Raman.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: ...Raman.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Meera is Raman's sister, Parth. She was six when he went into the tank.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: And you came here because of her. You told me that in cycle nineteen. You never stayed long enough to tell me why.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Now listen. Listen properly, for once. Everything in this place drains to the old reservoir.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: We drew it together, on the shower floor, with the handle of a spoon. Pump room under Maintenance. The sump. Then the culvert, under the wall.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Water knows the way out. It's the only thing in here that does.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Raman's sister. She thinks she's being kind to you. Maybe she even is. That's the worst part.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: She's waiting for something from you, Parth. She's been waiting {cycle_words} cycles. I would have given up at ten.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: I stopped swallowing the pills in cycle nine. Then my head stopped letting them in.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: So now they keep me behind glass and pretend I'm furniture. Furniture with an excellent memory.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Special Room B. Empty. Freshly mopped. Go and read the plate on the door.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: S-07. That's your number, yaar. They're making up your bed.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Everybody asks that by day two. Ask me better questions and I'll give you better answers.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Follow the water. And breathe the way the boy taught you. Two, seven, one, eight.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Rathore's master key. You actually went and got it.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Three years in a glass box. My knees have forgotten how to be knees.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Chal. You walk, I follow. I've always been following you around, that's the joke.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Go. I'll be here. I'm always here.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: Don't stop for me. I waited three years, I can wait for you to pick a door.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: And Parth. Whatever she asks you down there, answer it awake.

nodes.speaker: KABIR
nodes.text: So. We just walk out the front, like visitors? I'd like to see their faces.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: There you are. Sit, sit. Don't stand there like a guest.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: I won't keep you long. The bus back is at twelve, and the driver doesn't wait for anybody's mother.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: ...You used to.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: It doesn't matter, beta. I talk, you listen. That was always our arrangement.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: The rains came late this year. The whole village is complaining, as if complaining brings clouds.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: The mango tree behind the temple split down the middle. Half of it still gives fruit. Stubborn thing.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: And the old tank. They drained it, finally. After twenty-five years.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Nothing in it. Mud, and an iron grate at the bottom, all rusted through. Half the village went to look, like it was a fair.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: I didn't go. I couldn't.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: I brought this. I bring it every time.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Keep it. I have the negatives.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Eat properly. You've gone thin in the face again.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: You're looking at me like a stranger again. It's all right. I'm used to it.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Your father's cousin asked after you. I said you were working. They say you work in here, na? So it isn't a lie.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: The tank is still empty. Children dare each other to climb down the ladder. I told them there's nothing down there. I don't know why I said it like that.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: I brought another one. I always bring another one.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Next week. Same day, same time. Eat properly.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Go on, beta. They only give us the hour.

nodes.speaker: VISITOR
nodes.text: Keep the photo somewhere they won't find it.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: You sat down by yourself.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: In {cycle_words} cycles you have never once sat in that chair without two men holding your arms.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: I know who you are.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: You always know who I am, by the end. You never know why you came.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: I do now. I saw your name on a notice, and I signed.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to her?

choice.text: Beg her to wipe you again.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: Why did you keep going? All these cycles.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: Because on tape twelve you begged me to, and I said yes.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: And because for a few hours after every wipe you're not the boy who came back from the tank alone. You're a stranger in a cell. I can look at a stranger.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: I told myself I'd stop when you remembered why you came.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: So. Why did you come, Parth?

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: He didn't go in by himself.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: His foot caught in the grate, on the last eight. He grabbed my hand.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: I was out of air. I pulled my hand away, Meera. I let go of him.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: Then I stood in front of your mother, dripping, and I told her he went in alone.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: That's why I came. Not to forget it. To say it to you.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: Twenty-five years. {cycle_words_cap} cycles. That's the first time you've said it awake.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: I thought I'd feel something when I finally heard it.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: I don't know what this is.

nodes.speaker: PARTH
nodes.text: I can't carry it. Please. Make me forget.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: That's what you said on tape twelve. Word for word.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: ...Again, then.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: Every time.

nodes.speaker: MEERA
nodes.text: Go, then. You know the way out better than I do. You've drawn it on enough walls.
